title: The Eagle band and trombonist Frankie Dusen
summary: The Eagle band was a dance band led by Frankie Dusen, whom he first heard playing valve trombone when he was about 15 or 16; he describes his playing.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Did he ever play with the Eagle band? Do you remember?
Yeah, yeah.
Did you hear the Eagle band? Was it a dance band or street band?
Yeah, yeah, dance band. I heard the Eagle band.
Who had that band?
I believe... Frankie Duesen. That Eagle band.
What did he play at that time?
Who?
Frankie Duesen.
Trambo.
Sly?
Sly.
I thought maybe he played Val.
No, I never did know him to play with. It's the only one, the only one I know played Val Trambo and was... Harnished.
We just saw his wife this afternoon.
They were over there, yes? Yeah, yeah. We had a nice visit and she made a tape too like this. Talk about him.
When did he switch to the sliding trombone, Cornish?
Hmm?
When did Cornish switch to the sliding trombone?
I don't know. I don't know when he switched. I don't know the year or when.
He was playing Val when you first saw him?
Yeah, he was playing Val Trambo.
How old were you when you first saw him? Were you a little boy in short pants or were you grown?
No, I was a big boy. You know, I was about 16 or 15 years old around.
Did you ever work with him? Who Connish? Who Connish? Yeah, yeah. I was a little bit of a play.
What did he play like? Hmm? What did he play like? Was he a routine or was he a good one?
Yeah, yeah. He was a routine, but he could play pretty good.
Could he read some of the parts in the bands too already? Did he use music much on the parades when he played?
Yeah, yeah, yeah. He didn't use it.
